title: Literature and Stories
description: Type memorable passages, short stories, and literary ideas.

lessons.title: Silent Winter
lessons.text: The snow had folded every sharp edge of the world into a hush that felt both private and endless. Each step across the street sounded distant, as if the city had agreed to speak more softly for the night. In that silence, even small thoughts arrived with unusual clarity.

lessons.title: The Last Leaf
lessons.text:
1. THE ILLNESS
In a Greenwich Village artists' colony, a young painter named Johnsy catches pneumonia. Looking out her window at an ivy vine losing its leaves, she becomes convinced she will die when the last remaining leaf falls.

2. THE DESPERATE EFFORT
Her roommate Sue tries to cheer her up and confides in their downstairs neighbor, Old Behrman, an elderly painter who has dreamed for decades of painting a masterpiece. Behrman is fiercely protective of the young women and angered by Johnsy's morbid fantasy.

3. THE MASTERPIECE
After a night of severe wind and rain, the last leaf amazingly remains attached to the vine day after day. Inspiring Johnsy to regain her will to live, she recovers. Sue later reveals that Behrman died in the hospital: he went out into the cold storm to paint a realistic leaf on the wall, saving Johnsy's life with his true masterpiece.

lessons.title: The Cask of Amontillado
lessons.text:
1. THE ENTRAPMENT
Seeking vengeance against Fortunato for an unspecified insult, Montresor encounters his rival intoxicated during carnival season. Montresor lures Fortunato to his damp family catacombs by claiming to have acquired a rare cask of Amontillado wine.

2. THE JOURNEY DOWN
Montresor leads Fortunato deeper into the dark, bone-lined catacombs, using Fortunato's pride as a wine connoisseur and offering him drinks to keep him intoxicated.

3. THE ENTOMBMENT
Reaching the furthest niche, Montresor chains Fortunato to the wall. He then systematically lays brick and mortar to wall up the entrance. Ignoring Fortunato's screams and eventual silence, Montresor finishes the wall. Fifty years pass, and Montresor notes that the secret remains untouched.

lessons.title: The Lottery
lessons.text:
1. THE GATHERING
On a warm summer morning, residents of a small American village gather in the square for an annual June ritual known as 'the lottery.' Children collect smooth stones while families chat nervously around a worn black wooden box.

2. THE DRAWING
Mr. Summers conducts the drawing where the head of each household selects a folded slip of paper. Bill Hutchinson draws the slip with a black central mark. His wife, Tessie, begins shouting that the draw was unfair, but the family is subjected to a second drawing.

3. THE UNTHINKABLE RITUAL
Each family member draws a slip, and Tessie receives the paper with the black spot. The townsfolk, including her friends and young children, grab the gathered stones and surround her. Tessie screams 'It isn't fair, it isn't right!' as the town stones her to death to ensure a good harvest.

lessons.title: An Occurrence at Owl Creek Bridge
lessons.text:
1. THE EXECUTION
Peyton Farquhar, a wealthy Southern plantation owner during the Civil War, stands on a railroad bridge in Alabama with a noose around his neck, about to be hanged by Union soldiers for attempting to destroy the bridge.

2. THE IMPOSSIBLE ESCAPE
As the trap door drops, the rope snaps. Farquhar falls into the swift river, frees his tied hands, swims to safety under rifle fire, and flees into the dense forest. He walks all day and night through the wilderness toward his home.

3. THE REVELATION
He reaches his property and sees his wife stepping out to greet him with open arms. As he reaches to embrace her, a blinding white light flashes and a sharp shock hits his neck. Farquhar is dead, his neck broken below Owl Creek Bridge—his entire escape was an instant illusion before death.

lessons.title: The Open Window
lessons.text:
1. THE STORY BEGINS
Framton Nuttel, a man suffering from severe anxiety, arrives at a rural estate to rest his nerves. While waiting for the homeowner, Mrs. Sappleton, he is entertained by her 15-year-old niece, Vera.

2. THE TRAGIC TALE
Vera points to a large open French window and tells Framton that three years ago, Mrs. Sappleton's husband, brothers, and dog went hunting and drowned in a bog. She claims her aunt keeps the window open expecting them to walk back in.

3. THE PRANK
Mrs. Sappleton enters and mentions her husband will return soon. Moments later, three men with a dog walk across the lawn toward the window. Terrified that he is seeing ghosts, Framton flees the house in panic. Vera casually explains to her family that Framton ran off due to a phobia of dogs, showing her talent for tall tales on short notice.
